newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian minister says taxes stifle private sector.
newsitem.headline: Serbian minister says taxes stifle private sector.

text.p: Serbia's minister for private enterprise Radoje Djukic has criticised the federal and republican governments for stifling the private sector with high taxes, the Belgrade daily Nasa Borba reported on Tuesday.

"Unable to fill its budget, the state is very incorrectly and in an uncontrolled manner grabbing funds from private companies' accounts," Nasa Borba quoted Djukic as saying in talks with Serbian and Montenegrin officials and businessmen in the seaside resort of Budva.

Apparently breaking ranks with his fellow members of the Serbian socialist cabinet, Djukic said that by reimposing taxes on imports of new technology and equipment, abolished years ago, the federal government was "taxing foreign investment".
"This is a blow to the private sector. At this moment technology and equipment is not being imported by large (state-owned) firms since they are non-solvent," Djukic said.
He said Serbia was tolerating non-solvency and enormous losses incurred by the public and social sector.
"Ownership responsibility is nonexistent in that sector and we, as a state, are tolerating this," he said.
Djukic said there was resistance at all levels to privatisation in Serbia, which was lagging far behind Montenegro in the process.
"But no-one will stop the private sector, nor privatisation which is in progress," Djukic said, adding that it could only be slowed down.
